name: Atypical Chronic Myeloid Leukemia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO 2016 Diagnostic Criteria for Atypical Chronic Myeloid Leukemia

criteria.description: Persistent leukocytosis with >10% immature granulocytes in peripheral blood
Absence of BCR-ABL1 fusion gene by molecular testing
Presence of dysgranulopoiesis in bone marrow and peripheral blood
Blasts in peripheral blood and bone marrow less than 20%
Peripheral blood monocytes less than 10% of leukocytes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All major criteria must be met, including leukocytosis with >10% immature granulocytes, absence of BCR-ABL1 fusion gene, and dysgranulopoiesis; blasts must be less than 20% and monocytes less than 10%.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other myeloid neoplasms, especially chronic myeloid leukemia and chronic myelomonocytic leukemia.

laboratory: Leukocytosis with left shift and dysplastic granulocytes
Absence of Philadelphia chromosome and BCR-ABL1 fusion gene
imaging: Splenomegaly on abdominal ultrasound or CT
other: Bone marrow biopsy showing hypercellularity with granulocytic proliferation and dysplasia

distinguishingFeatures: More pronounced dysplasia in multiple lineages

redFlags: Rapid increase in peripheral blood blasts >20%
Severe anemia or thrombocytopenia causing bleeding or organ dysfunction
Signs of leukostasis such as neurological deficits or respiratory distress
